title: throughput-benchmarking-harness-and-methodology-guidelines
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures the recommended harness and methodology we use for throughput-focused experiments on the serving runtime. Focus is on reproducible load generation, warmup practices (KV cache/activation), measurement windows, and artifacts to capture for investigations and PRs. It is intentionally prescriptive to reduce flakiness when comparing kernel changes, batching strategies, and routing policies.

High-level goals:
- Measure stable tokens/sec and request-level tail latency under controlled input distributions.
- Maximize repeatability across runs (hardware/driver variance minimized).
- Produce artifact bundle sufficient to diagnose regressions (raw traces, GPU metrics, loadgen config).

Harness architecture (brief):
- Controller node: orchestrates experiments, uploads configs, collects metrics.
- Load generators: stateless processes that drive traffic (we typically run 4-16 RGs per test depending on throughput target).
- Metrics collectors: Prometheus exporters + nvidia-smi aggregator + perf counters.
- Tracing: optional jaeger/zipkin span capture for selected runs.

Workload design and inputs:
- Input shapes: standardize on a small set of canonical shapes:
  * short-chat: 32 tokens prompt, 64 tokens response target
  * long-completion: 512 tokens prompt, 512 tokens response target
  * embeddings: variable length, use fixed 256-token sample set
- Sequence length distribution: prefer synthetic mixtures (80% short, 20% long) that approximate product traffic for PLG customers.
- Model variants: always record exact model hash / tokenizer version.

Load generator configs (recommended fields):
- mode: concurrency | closed_loop_qps | poisson
- target_qps: numeric (when using qps mode)
- concurrency: numeric (when using concurrency mode)
- max_inflight_per_conn: usually 16
- request_timeout_ms: 120000
- think_time_ms: per-request pause (set 0 for pure saturation)
- seed: RNG seed string for deterministic sampling of prompts

Traffic shapes explained:
- concurrency mode: best for saturating internal batching layers and measuring max throughput. Use increasing concurrency ramp.
- closed_loop_qps: emulate client-limited QPS; good for realistic latency curves.
- poisson (or ramping poisson): introduce stochasticity; helps exercise burst handling and scheduler paths.

Warmup and priming rules:
- Warmup must be explicit and included in run artifacts. Do not measure during warmup window.
- Warmup goals: populate KV cache, JIT kernels, initial CUDA context allocation, and steady thermal state.
- Recommended warmup procedure:
  1) Short priming (5 minutes at 25% of target load) to trigger lazy initializations.
  2) Main warmup (10-20 minutes at 50-75% of target) to stabilize batching behavior and CUDA memory patterns.
  3) Final ramp to target over 2 minutes.
- For models with large KV caches, include a prompt-set sweep as part of warmup to populate relevant KV entries.

Repeatability checklist (to include with every experiment):
- hardware_snapshot: GPU model, driver, CUDA/cuDNN versions, BIOS, OS kernel version
- container_image: full sha256 of runtime image
- git_commit: serving runtime + model loader commit SHAs
- loadgen_config: full config file (include RNG seed)
- start_time_utc and timezone
- temperature/thermal baseline if available (or note if lab environment)
- prometheus scrape interval and retention settings

Measurement windows and metrics:
- Ignore warmup window. Measure at least 5 minutes at stable target, prefer 10 minutes for tail stability.
- Primary metrics: tokens/sec (aggregate), requests/sec, p50/p95/p99/p999 latency (server-side), GPU utilization (per device), GPU power draw, CPU steal/steal time, host load, memory pressure, network RX/TX.
- Secondary metrics: batch size distribution, queue depth, kernel execution times, KV cache hit rate.
- Save histograms (not just percentiles) to allow re-computation of percentiles.

Artifacts to collect and attach to PRs/investigations:
- loadgen_config.yaml (text)
- raw loadgen logs (rotated)
- prometheus raw scrape snapshots for the experiment window
- GPU traces (nsight or nvidia-smi logs) when diagnosing kernel-level regressions
- runtime traces (structured logs with request ids)
- batch size distributions and sampled request payloads (anonymized)

Common pitfalls and mitigation:
- Docker CPU quotas can throttle loadgen or server process; use host networking and avoid CPU cgroups when possible.
- Non-deterministic input sampling: always set seed in loadgen and include the seed in artifacts.
- Thermal throttling: run a baseline thermal test and annotate runs; schedule long runs during stable datacenter hours.
- Background processes (profilers, system updates) can skew results; run on a dedicated test host or pinned CPUs.

Debugging workflow when variance observed:
1) Re-run with identical config and seed once to confirm flakiness.
2) If variance persists, capture a short kernel tracing run (2-3 minutes) with increased debug logs.
3) Compare batch distributions between runs to see if batching heuristics changed.
4) Check GPU clocks/power; if clocks vary, add BIOS-level stability test.

Quick examples (commands and YAML snippets):
- Example loadgen invocation:
  ./loadgen --config configs/short-chat-poisson.yaml --out artifacts/run-2026-02-25 --seed 12345

- Minimal config (short-chat-poisson.yaml):
  mode: poisson
  target_qps: 1200
  concurrency: null
  sequence_profile: short-chat
  duration_s: 900
  warmup_s: 900
  seed: 12345

Acceptance criteria for a stable throughput benchmark run:
- p99 variance across three independent runs < 5% while running identical configs
- aggregate tokens/sec within 3% between runs
- no GPU thermal/power capping events during measurement window

Reporting and dashboarding:
- Standard dashboard should plot tokens/sec, request/sec, p50/p95/p99/p999, GPU utilization, batch size heatmap, and KV cache hit rate.
- Annotate runs with commit SHAs and config links for quick triage.

Versioning and naming conventions for artifacts:
- run-YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<short-description>-<git-sha>.tar.gz (tar contains all artifacts above)
- config files kept alongside harness repo under configs/ named with the run id

Open items / TODOs:
- Add automated detection of non-stationary GPU clocks and fail the run if clocks fluctuate beyond threshold.
- Add a small embedded benchmark for model warmup time so we can compare cold-start penalty across kernels.
- Improve anonymization tooling for sampled payloads.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a living doc; suggestions welcome for additional canonical input shapes and acceptance thresholds for new instances. If you run a benchmark that differs from these guidelines, please attach reasoning in the PR or bug.

End of doc.
